evidence.quoted_text:
base.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        require(not base.stat().st_mode & 0o077,
                "private record directory must have mode 0700: " + str(base))
        name = ("run-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime())
                + "-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6])
        self.run_dir = base / name
        self.run_dir.mkdir(mode=0o700)
evidence.reason: `claim_run_dir` creates the record base and the new run directory but never fsyncs the record base after creating the run-directory entry. `durable_write(path, receipt)` can make the receipt file and its containing run directory durable, but it cannot make the new directory entry in the parent record base durable. A power loss after admission can therefore leave the host held while losing the run directory and its recovery state. This is a routine crash-consistency defect, not a new contract requirement; the fix is to fsync the record base after `mkdir` (and its parent if the base was created), refusing admission on failure.
